newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine committee sets draft job emergency bill.
newsitem.headline: Argentine committee sets draft job emergency bill.

text.p: The labor and pension committees of Argentina's lower house of Congress released a draft bill Wednesday that would declare an "employment emergency" reducing employers' burden in paying benefits.
The bill would give employers two years' grace to hire new workers with six-month contracts, renewable for up to two years, on reduced social benefits.

Argentina's Peronist government has put before Congress legislation that would loosen labor laws, scrapping collective bargaining and making workers' hours more flexible. It has threatened to implement it by decree by the end of this year if Congress fails to pass it.
Under the draft bill released Wednesday, companies would during the first six months have to provide family allowance, health plan contributions and work safety insurance.

If the contract is renewed for another six months, companies would have to pay these as well as 25 percent of pension benefits. Contracts of up to 18 months would require employers to pay 50 percent of pension contributions.
The plan would also create a layoff fund, four percent of which would be financed by companies -- 3.8 percent going to workers' private pension schemes and 0.2 percent to a common fund.
